title: Dama ben Netina
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Kiddushin 31a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.31a.9-10) relates that a gentile in Ashkelon named Dama ben Netina honored his father. Once, the Sages of Israel (during the Temple period) came to buy stones for the ephod from him. The keys lay beneath his father’s head, and he refused to wake him. God rewarded him with a red heifer born in his herd; for it he obtained all the profit from the stones that he had forgone for his father’s sake.[^1]

notes.text: The linked Bavli places the key under Dama’s father’s head. In the parallel in [Jerusalem Talmud Peah 1:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Peah.1.1.22), it lies in his father’s fingers, or his father’s foot rests on the chest. The Bavli sets the heifer’s birth the following year. The Yerushalmi sets it that very night.
